entities.summary:
Eljigidei Noyan was a Mongol commander in Persia, instrumental in the expansion of the Mongol Empire under Genghis Khan's successors.

Born into a family of high-ranking officials, Eljigidei rose through the ranks of the Mongol military, playing a crucial role in the defeat of the Khwarezmid Empire in 1221.

His military campaigns in Persia were marked by brutal suppression and strategic brilliance, as he successfully implemented Genghis Khan's 'Yassa' code to maintain order and discipline among the Mongol forces.

Eljigidei's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also played a key role in the administration of the Mongol Empire, serving as a governor and advisor to the Great Khan.

Eljigidei's life and military campaigns were immortalized in the Mongolian epic poem, the 'Yassa', which chronicles the conquests and exploits of the Mongol warriors.

In the annals of history, Eljigidei's name stands as a testament to the Mongol Empire's unparalleled military prowess and administrative efficiency.
